catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-7.explanation: age groupsBut in the USA, skydiving is a hobby that has been taken up by people from all age groups...

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-8.explanation: (university) studentSo, my first jump was as a university student – when I was able to get a discount.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-9.explanation: heightsOf course, some people start skydiving to help them get over a fear of heights.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-10.explanation: websitesSo, how do you start? The equipment for skydiving is specialised, and not easy to get in local sports shops. Nowadays, most people buy skydiving kit from websites – there’s more choice and you can see photographs.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-13.explanation: airportIf you’re interested, you need to get in touch with the Parachute Association, and you’ll find the contact details through your local airport.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-14.explanation: several monthsThey’ll give advice on how to get started. You can learn to skydive over a weekend, but I suggest the best way is to do it over several months - that allows you to build up your confidence gradually. Skydiving’s great. It’ll give you a whole new outlook on life!

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-15.explanation: CRoger Moffat: Well, about ten years ago I had a heart by-pass operation and about the same time I was made redundant. I was feeling pretty low at the time, so I decided that the only thing to do was to take my working life into my own hands and set up my own business.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-16.explanation: BRoger Moffat: You could say it was a bit like taking a roller-coaster ride and wondering when you were going to come flying off at break-neck speed! Everything was a challenge: finance, production, marketing.

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-17.explanation: DRoger Moffat: To be honest, none at all. I feel that I’ve escaped being a slave to a regular income, from commuting, from having to justify my actions to everyone, from having to attend the office party...

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-18.explanation: ARoger Moffat: No more than anyone else. I mean, there’s no job security anywhere these days, is there?

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-19.explanation: BRoger Moffat: I think I’m a bit of an oddball character really. I suppose you might say that I was a hard-headed romantic. I believe that an engineer has to invent ideas. You need to be very talented. You need to have a feeling for balance and form. You also need to feel you have status and that people value what you’re doing. I’ve always seen engineers as sort of visionaries, if you like

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-20.explanation: BRoger Moffat: To me, mechanical things are magical: a motor car is a thrilling bit of science. The microchip is a masterpiece of theoretical design; machines of unbelievable complexity make them. But from my point of view, the most rewarding thing of all is that all these things are designed by engineers

catalog-listening-cae-c1-test8-q-22.explanation: F I have to admit that I was one of those awful people who used to tell others to do something that I didn’t do myself. It wasn’t until I was invited to present a report on [22] a conference in the USA, and I was sceptical before that too, that I came back a convert. There’s good research to show that people are healthier if they eat breakfast, and everything I heard was quite convincing and I’ve gone on to use quite a lot of it in my column...
